Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the following sentence.

Rimjhim received a children's very illustrated colourful atlas on her 10th birthday.
o: a very illustrated colourful atlas children
a very colourful illustrated children's atlas
an very illustrated colourful children's atlas
a colourful very illustrated children's atlas
questions.s:
· The correct structure for adjectives is:

Quantity → Opinion → Size → Age → Shape → Colour → Origin → Material → Purpose → Noun

· Correct phrase: "a very colourful illustrated children's atlas"

· Incorrect options:

o A) Misplaces adjectives.

o C) Uses "an" incorrectly (before consonant sound).

o D) Adjective order is incorrect.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

He dreams big than his friends.
questions.s:
The underlined word 'big' is in a positive degree but in the sentence, the dreams of the subject are compared with those of his friends and so the sentence is in a comparative degree which means the adjective 'big' has to be in comparative form. Among the given options, 'biggest' is the superlative form and cannot be used. 'More big' and 'most big' are incorrect by default because when a proper comparative/superlative degree adjective exists, we use that instead of making a comparative/superlative degree adjective using 'more/most' and so they are also negated. Option (a) 'bigger' is the most appropriate word that is in comparative form and can replace the underlined word in the given sentence.

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

Note:

· The Positive Degree of an Adjective is the Adjective in its simple form. It is used to denote the mere existence of some quality of what we speak about. It is used when no comparison is made.

· The Comparative degree of an adjective denotes a higher degree of quality than the positive and is used when two things are compared.

· The Superlative degree indicates the highest degree of quality and is used when more than two things (or sets of things) are compared.

questions.q:
Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.

Life in (more) thriving towns is intimately connected with the local trades and industries.
questions.s:
The correct answer is option 3.

Here, the superlative form of the adjective(in this specific case, a determiner) 'many' has been used to signify that life in almost all thriving towns is intimately connected with the local trades and industries.

Much' is an adjective of the positive degree generally used to qualify uncountable nouns, which clearly is not the case here. A 'town' is a countable noun. 

Note: Many>More>Most (increase in degree as we move from left to right)

questions.q: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select No improvement required.
o: at a more leisurely paced
at a more leisurely pace
at a more leisure paced
No improvement needed
questions.s:
Correct Answer: at a more leisurely pace

Explanation:
The phrase "leisure pace" is incorrect because "leisure" is a noun and cannot directly describe "pace". The correct adjective form is "leisurely", which means unhurried or relaxed.

Let’s evaluate the options:

  • at a more leisurely paced – ❌ Incorrect; "paced" is an adjective but does not fit after "a more" and before "pace".

  • at a more leisurely pace – ✅ Correct; grammatically sound and idiomatically appropriate.

  • at a more leisure paced – ❌ Incorrect; "leisure" cannot be used as an adjective this way.

  • No improvement needed – ❌ Incorrect; improvement is clearly required.

Correct sentence:
"Although uncountable files stack up on the tables of government officials, they prefer doing their work at a more leisurely pace."
